decisions.reason: Reject unqualified cross-grain equality. Order item prices reconcile to pretax subtotal, while order_total adds tax. The pinned seeds differ by 3,398,137 cents overall, with nonzero tax on 61,465 orders.
Agreed: first-customer-order filter restricts the same SUM(1) base order measure.
Agreed: order-value threshold restricts the same SUM(1) base order measure.
Agreed: food condition changes the population contributing product price to the same SUM measure.
Apply the scope-variant rule consistently to two sibling category predicates over the same product_price SUM, even when neither category is a subset of the other. They are not interchangeable.
Agreed: SUM versus MEDIAN changes the aggregation function over the same price column.

The values count different entities, but the repository models a direct customer-to-order relationship and derives orders per customer. Under this taxonomy, that is related, not an unrelated nonmatch.
Agreed on distinct tax-inclusive and pretax amounts. The model explicitly sums tax_paid; a location tax-rate reconstruction is unnecessary and has not been validated.
Agreed: customer count and average store tax rate have unrelated entities and units.

Revise the first analyst's needs_review label. All-time totals reconcile in the pinned seeds when every order maps to a customer, but default time dimensions are ordered_at versus first_ordered_at; daily values differ on all 365 sample dates. A cross-grain claim is conditional on dropping or aligning time and validating mapping.
